steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with salted water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes. Drain.
Meanwhile, bring a medium saucepan of water to a boil; add peas and simmer until just tender, about 6 to 7 minutes. Drain and set peas aside.

Add butter to the same saucepan; melt over medium heat. Stir in flour to make a thick paste; gradually whisk in milk, stirring constantly until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Add potatoes and peas; simmer, stirring often, until potatoes are heated through, about 5 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamed Peas and New Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This creamed peas and potato recipe is easy to make with minimal ingredients. It’s so tasty — it might become your go-to recipe for new potatoes.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is AWESOME!!!!! Simple and incredibly inexpensive to make (only *5* main ingredients + all of them can be purchased in large quantities for very little money = not too shabby!). I made a big pot of this meal for less than $10. You can't beat it for the amount of rich flavor you get out of this easy recipe. You won't be disappointed (I could praise this dish all day!). I can't wait to stop being full so I can eat more of it. I will definitely be making this again. SUGGESTIONS ----------------- -Triple or quadruple this recipe because you will want to share it with everyone you know! Plus, it makes for great leftovers. -Before adding potatoes to sauce with peas, mash the peas in the sauce or put the peas in a food processor and give a slight chop on them before adding to sauce. -Season with salt (black truffle finishing salt works great), fresh coarsely ground pepper, and a generous amount of turmeric. It will change your life. :) -I used medium russet potatoes (which are less than $5 for a huge bag) and had no flavor issues. Baby red potatoes probably would have added to the flavor, but I didn't feel like running to the store to make that kind of commitment. -I honestly don't know what shelled English peas are, but I used store-brand frozen peas and everything was terrific.
I made this recipe in my slow cooker. Less pots and utensils to wash. No boiling hot pots of water to handle. I added some cream with the milk. Makes a delicious white sauce for bread dipping.

Want to take this recipe from Wow to WOW? Use half sweet potatoes and half red potatoes. I cooked my potatoes in salted water just until barely tender. I doubled the sauce and added a bit of sugar to it and cooked it down a little thicker. I also added more peas.. because I love peas! I used frozen peas and just added them to the drained potatoes, then I added the cream sauce. PERFECTION!
This is a garden harvest favorite when the baby red potatoes and freah peas are ready I add sauteed thin sliced garden onion to the butter as well...yumo!

This a variation to Creamed Peas and New Potatoes my family has enjoyed for years. Of course is it best with fresh peas and new baby potatoes, but frozen peas and any potatoes will work.
What I do: Cook the peas, potatoes and chopped onion (about 1/2 Cup) in in a covered sauce pan with just enough water (about 1/2 cup) so it doesn't scorch until the potatoes are tender. Remove from heat and drain reserving cooking water. Add this water to milk (fat free half & half works great) so you have 1 cup. Follow step 3 in the recipe. Adding a slice of american cheese gives it an added richness.
If have peas with edible pods, these are great and add some extra pea flavor. Just chop them to the size you desire.
This is a good, basic recipe that has spanned the generations. When fresh peas are out of season, I just add frozen peas to the boiling potatoes 4-5 minutes before the potatoes are done. Good stuff.

My grandmother (who was born in 1883!) used to make this as soon as the new potatoes were ready. She always added dillweed and a few pearl onions, so I did, too. Wonderful and great memories!

There is no flavor to this recipe my husband said I would have been fine with just potatoes and peas !!!! I made it a second time thinking I can fix this fried bacon then sauté onion garlic salt pepper added some butter to bacon greese added tbsp flour cooked it to paste added milk slow wisk added potatoes peas to sauce took off heat sprinkle bacon no flavor

My mother and both my grandmother's would make this as soon as the peas and potatoes started coming on in the garden. It is definitely comfort food for me! Sometimes they would add small onions from the garden also. Good, basic recipe. I make it several times during the spring and summer. ☀️

Made this tonight and it was wonderful. I mostly followed the recipe exactly but added 1-2 tbsp chopped onion sauteed in the butter + an extra tbsp, a little s&p, and a sprinkle of turmeric, and a small amount, 1/2 tsp minced garlic. Lovely! Judi D.
Love this recipe it’s just like what my mom used to make. It’s great with new potatoes and peas in the spring, but I make it year-round. It’s so good.
A delish recipe that is easy to make and different than the usual mashed potatoes. Goes with any main dish from meat to fish.
I love this recipe, I make it every spring , but I like a thicker sauce, but either way delicious
Added turmeric and more butter. Used green beans instead of peas.
I make this often sometimes using frozen peas. Easy and delicious.
very good recipe, thats me back to when my Mom made this.
Simply put is great!

My Grandmother and Mother use to make this as I was growing up. I loved it. They both are gone, I wanted to make it, but did not have the recipe. I remember them making it and it tasted just slightly sweet. So the only changes I made was about a teaspoon of sugar. I made a lot more than this recipe gives, we like leftovers. This is a side dish, peas and potatoes are the main ingredient, so expect this flavor. The cream just adds to the two. Highly recommend as a change up to your side dishes.
So very easy to make, I actually did one pot just kept the boiled potatoes warm while making the cream sauce.
